title: analogRead
summary: To capture analog values in software, Arduino provides the built-in function analogRead():

steps.title: analogRead

quickCheck.question: Is it mandatory to declare pinMode(A0, INPUT) in setup() before calling analogRead(A0)?
options: No, analogRead() automatically configures the internal ADC multiplexer for that pin
Yes, omitting pinMode causes a compilation error
Yes, pinMode must be set to OUTPUT
quickCheck.explanation: Analog pins automatically configure their internal ADC circuitry upon calling `analogRead()`, so `pinMode` is optional.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The Arduino core automatically configures analog pins when `analogRead()` is invoked.

quickCheck.question: If analogRead(A0) returns a reading of approximately 512, what voltage is present on pin A0?
quickCheck.explanation: 512 is halfway between 0 and 1023, representing exactly half of 5.0V (2.5V).
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: 512 / 1023 is approximately 50%, which corresponds to 2.5V out of 5.0V.

questions.question: What range of integer values does analogRead() return on an Uno?
questions.explanation: 10-bit analogRead() produces numbers from 0 (0V) up to 1023 (5V)!

questions.question: What reading does analogRead() return if an analog pin is connected directly to 5V?
questions.explanation: Full supply voltage (5.0V) reaches the maximum 10-bit ADC value: 1023!
